---
title: "Data and quality control"
subtitle: "Do the samples group as expected?"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("_common.R")
lib_million <- colSums(counts_raw) / 1e6
wt_inf <- grepl("^wt_infected", names(lib_million))
repl <- qc[, .(lo = min(mean_dist_replicates), hi = max(mean_dist_replicates)),
           by = .(wt_inf = group == "wt_infected")]
low <- qc[, .(lo = min(share_filtered_genes_below_5_counts),
              hi = max(share_filtered_genes_below_5_counts)),
          by = .(wt_inf = group == "wt_infected")]
```

## Data

The counts come from GEO series
[GSE133329](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE133329), deposited with the
study of Schmidt et al. ([PNAS 2019](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1907031116)). A TRIM28 knockout
clone of A549 lung epithelial cells was reconstituted with wild-type TRIM28 (wt) or with TRIM28 6KR,
a mutant whose six SUMOylation sites are replaced. Cells were mock treated or infected with IAV
A/WSN/33 at a multiplicity of infection of 10 for 6 hours, with three replicates per group. The
12 count tables contain `r n(nrow(counts_raw))` genes.

**Genes were kept when they had at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples**, 3 being the size of the
smallest group. This keeps genes that are switched on in a single condition, and it uses no group
labels, which matters later: the filter is applied once to all samples before the
cross-validation of the Random Forest, so it must not carry label information into the test
sample. The filter kept `r n(n_tested)` of `r n(nrow(counts_raw))` genes.

## Infection separates the samples first, the genotype second

Counts were transformed with the regularised logarithm (rlog) of DESeq2 in blind mode, so that no
group information enters the transformation. On the 500 most variable genes, the first principal
component separates infected from mock samples and carries `r f1(pca_var[1])` % of the variance,
the second separates the genotypes (`r f1(pca_var[2])` %). Hover over a point to see the sample.

```{r}
#| label: pca
#| fig-cap: "Principal component analysis of the 500 most variable genes after rlog transformation. Interactive: hover for sample name and library size, click a legend entry to hide a group."
pca <- copy(qc)
pca[, group_label := factor(GROUP_LABELS[group], levels = GROUP_LABELS)]
pca[, hover := sprintf("<b>%s</b><br>%.1f million reads", sample, library_size / 1e6)]
plot_ly(pca, x = ~PC1, y = ~PC2, color = ~group_label, colors = unname(GROUP_COLOURS),
        text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text", type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(size = 13, line = list(width = 1, color = "white"))) |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f %% variance)", pca_var[1])),
         yaxis = list(title = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f %% variance)", pca_var[2])),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "Group"))) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE)
```

![Study design and sample structure. **a**, The 2 × 2 design. **b**, PCA as above. **c**, Euclidean distances between samples on all `r n(n_tested)` filtered genes, clustered by average linkage; darker blue means more similar.](assets/figures/figure_1.png){fig-alt="Design table, PCA and sample distance heatmap" width="90%"}

## Is there an outlier?

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-8}
On all filtered genes, the wt-infected replicates are further apart from each other (mean distance
to their replicates `r f1(repl[wt_inf == TRUE, lo])`–`r f1(repl[wt_inf == TRUE, hi])`) than the
replicates of the other groups (`r f1(repl[wt_inf == FALSE, lo])`–`r f1(repl[wt_inf == FALSE, hi])`).
These three samples also have the smallest libraries
(`r f1(min(lib_million[wt_inf]))`–`r f1(max(lib_million[wt_inf]))` million reads, against
`r f1(min(lib_million[!wt_inf]))`–`r f1(max(lib_million[!wt_inf]))` million in the other groups) and
the highest share of filtered genes with fewer than 5 counts
(`r f1(100 * low[wt_inf == TRUE, lo])`–`r f1(100 * low[wt_inf == TRUE, hi])` % against
`r f1(100 * low[wt_inf == FALSE, lo])`–`r f1(100 * low[wt_inf == FALSE, hi])` %). **The spread therefore most
likely reflects noise in weakly expressed genes rather than a failed sample**, and on the 500 most
variable genes the four groups still form four separate clusters. All 12 samples were kept, and the
noisier wt-infected group is named as a limitation.
:::
